findings.title: Immediate-retry metric counts unrelated rapid updates
findings.what: The report contract describes immediateRetries as failed attempts retried within one hour, but the loop increments for any consecutive pair whose timestamp gap is below one hour. Two successful updates 30 minutes apart, or a failure followed by another failure, are therefore reported as an immediate retry. This can overstate update instability and any recommendation based on that metric.
findings.fix: Increment only when the preceding record is unsuccessful and the following record represents the intended retry outcome, with finite non-negative timestamps and a gap below one hour.
findings.acceptance: Add cases containing success→success, failure→failure, success→failure, failure→success, invalid timestamps, and out-of-order input; only a chronologically consecutive failure→success pair with a finite 0-to-<1-hour gap increments immediateRetries.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/parse-last-update.ts:181-187 and the defining contract at lines 110-113. The condition checks only dt < one hour and never checks either outcome, so a reproducible two-success input 30 minutes apart returns immediateRetries=1 despite containing no failed attempt.
